## ✨ What's in 1.0

Cindl 1.0 is the first stable release: one client for your own
[Hermes Agent](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent), on the web, on
Linux and Windows, and on Android. It connects to your existing `hermes serve`,
signs in through Hermes's own sign-in, and adds no model, keys, accounts,
analytics or hosted service.

- **Conversations.** A main conversation and side conversations, with replies
  streamed as Hermes writes them. You can keep sending while Hermes works.
- **Approvals and questions, answered once.** Allow once or deny; Cindl never
  sends a standing grant, and never answers a sudo or secret prompt.
- **The working margin.** Beside each conversation: what it waits on, the
  step you selected, and the agent's computer.
- **The agent's computer.** Watch Hermes's own screen live, take control when
  you need to, and give it back.
- **Skills, memory and SOUL.** Read and edit them, each edit after reviewing a
  diff and against the version you read.
- **Your Hermes only.** Tokens stay in the system keyring on the desktop and in
  the Android Keystore; the web client uses Hermes's own session cookie.

## ⬇️ Install

| File                                    | For                                                                                                                                                           |
| --------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Cindl-1.0.0-x86_64.AppImage`           | Linux x64. Make it executable and run it.                                                                                                                     |
| `Cindl-Setup-1.0.0.exe`                 | Windows x64. Not code-signed: SmartScreen asks first, so choose **More info**, then **Run anyway**.                                                           |
| `cindl-1.0.0-android.apk`               | Android 7.0 or later. Allow installs from your browser if Android asks.                                                                                       |
| `cindl-web-1.0.0.tar`, `cindl-serve.py` | The web client, served by your Hermes host at `/cindl/`. See [Running Cindl](https://github.com/FlintSH/cindl/blob/v1.0.0/docs/handbook/operations/index.md). |

Then enter your Hermes address and sign in on Hermes's own page. Cindl is
verified against Hermes v0.22.5; newer versions connect and show as outside
that baseline.

### Verify

`SHA256SUMS` lists every file. The APK is signed with this certificate:

```text
SHA-256: A4:10:5F:20:F7:FA:59:01:03:5E:B0:8D:B2:2E:02:CC:84:02:B9:22:F5:9D:77:D7:9E:53:2A:92:0E:2B:B9:B6
```

Check it with `apksigner verify --print-certs cindl-1.0.0-android.apk`. Future
updates are signed with the same key.

## ⚠️ Known limits

- The AppImage and the Windows installer are not code-signed.
- The desktop app keeps tokens in memory only when the system has no keyring,
  so you sign in again after a restart.
- Everything is tested against a fake Hermes in CI, on an Android emulator and
  on both desktop builds; the [acceptance matrix](https://github.com/FlintSH/cindl/blob/v1.0.0/docs/handbook/project/acceptance-matrix.md)
  lists what each part has been checked against and the small follow-ups left.
